name: Hereditary Hemolytic Anemia Due to Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase Mediterranean Variant

criteria.description: Reduced glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase enzyme activity in red blood cells
Identification of Mediterranean variant mutation in the G6PD gene
Episodic hemolytic anemia triggered by oxidative stress (e.g., infections, certain drugs, fava beans)
Peripheral blood smear showing bite cells and Heinz bodies during hemolytic episodes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of reduced G6PD enzyme activity and identification of Mediterranean variant mutation with clinical history of hemolytic episodes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be complicated by normal enzyme levels during remission; testing during or shortly after hemolytic episodes is recommended.

pathognomonic.notes: Triggered by oxidative stress such as infections, drugs, or fava bean ingestion
searchTerms: episodes of sudden red blood cell breakdown

pathognomonic.notes: Due to increased bilirubin from red cell breakdown
searchTerms: jaundice during red blood cell breakdown attacks
skin yellowing during blood cell destruction

common.symptomName: Fatigue and pallor during hemolytic episodes
searchTerms: tiredness and pale skin during hemolysis
fatigue and pallor in anemia episodes
weakness and paleness during red cell loss
dark urine from blood cell breakdown
hemoglobin in urine causing dark color

common.notes: Mild to moderate enlargement during or after hemolytic episodes

searchTerms: tachycardia with low red blood cells

occasional.notes: Likely due to anemia and hypoxia
searchTerms: headache during blood cell destruction episodes
small areas of spleen tissue death

rare.symptomName: Severe acute hemolytic crisis with acute renal failure
searchTerms: severe hemolytic crisis with kidney failure
blood cell destruction leading to kidney injury

rare.symptomName: Aplastic crisis triggered by parvovirus B19 infection
searchTerms: temporary bone marrow failure from parvovirus
anemia crisis triggered by viral infection

rare.symptomName: Chronic hemolytic anemia with persistent jaundice
searchTerms: long-term red blood cell breakdown with jaundice

laboratory: Decreased G6PD enzyme activity in red blood cells
Elevated reticulocyte count during hemolytic episodes
Elevated indirect bilirubin and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH)
Peripheral blood smear showing bite cells and Heinz bodies
imaging: Splenic enlargement on abdominal imaging during crises
genetic: Identification of G6PD Mediterranean variant mutation (e.g., c.563C>T, p.Ser188Phe)
other: Positive family history consistent with X-linked inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of spherocytes on blood smear

redFlags: Severe acute hemolytic anemia with rapid hemoglobin drop
Acute renal failure during hemolytic crisis
Aplastic crisis with severe anemia and reticulocytopenia
references: Luzzatto L, Nannelli C, Notaro R. Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency. Hematol Oncol Clin North Am. 2016;30(2):373-393.
Cappellini MD, Fiorelli G. Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency. Lancet. 2008;371(9606):64-74.
